issues.description: Directs() still dereferences i.publicEnd in closure when i is nil
issues.detail: In ir_imports.go Directs(), the guard creates a nil-safe slice, but the closure captures `i` and reads `i.publicEnd` and `i.weakEnd` (via `public := n < i.publicEnd`). If `i == nil` this is safe only because the slice is empty so the closure never fires — fragile and easy to break. Consider asserting len(slice)==0 path or capturing values locally.

issues.description: AllMembers() returns iterator that captures nil seq, may not be safe
issues.detail: In ir_file.go AllMembers(), when f is nil, `raw` is a nil iter.Seq passed to iterx.Map. If iterx.Map ranges over a nil Seq it could panic on iteration depending on implementation. Verify iterx.Map handles nil Seq, or substitute an empty seq explicitly. The test only checks Len if present; iter.Seq has no Len so this path isn't exercised by the zero test.

issues.description: DescriptorProto() on empty imports may still surface zero imported but masks errors
issues.detail: `imports.DescriptorProto()` returns `imported.file` from slicesx.Last; when files is empty this returns a zero `imported` and `.file` is nil — fine. But the new nil guard returns nil only when i itself is nil; an empty (but non-nil) `imports` still uses slicesx.Last. Behavior is consistent but the nil-pointer branch is the only new guard; consider documenting both zero paths.

issues.description: Element.ValueNodeIndex sentinel -1 is a behavior change worth documenting more loudly
issues.detail: Returning -1 for zero Element is a new public API contract. Doc comment mentions it briefly but downstream code that previously assumed non-negative indices (e.g., `MessageKeys().At(idx)`) will panic if a zero Element is accidentally fed through. Consider noting callers must check IsZero before using the index.

issues.description: Reflection-based test skips function-returning accessors silently
issues.detail: In zero_test.go testZeroAny, returns of Kind Func are `continue`d, meaning accessors like iter.Seq[T] (function types) are not validated at all. The AllMembers path returns iter.Seq which would be skipped, so a panicking iterator wouldn't be caught by this test. Consider invoking the seq once to confirm it yields zero elements.

issues.description: Repeated nil-guard boilerplate across File methods invites drift
issues.detail: ir_file.go now has ~10 near-identical `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field }` blocks. A small helper (e.g., `fileSlice(f, func(*File) []T)`) would reduce footgun risk when adding new accessors and keep the nil contract uniform. Minor maintainability concern only.

review.summary: The PR adds a reflective zero-value test for the ir package and patches numerous accessors to no-panic on nil/zero receivers. The defensive guards are mostly mechanical and correct, but a few subtle holes remain: the Directs closure still touches receiver fields, AllMembers passes a nil iter.Seq through iterx.Map without verifying safety, and the reflective test silently skips function-typed returns so iterator accessors aren't actually exercised. Element.ValueNodeIndex now returns -1 as a sentinel — a public API contract worth flagging. Overall direction is good; tighten the test coverage and the two iteration paths before merge.
